record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove a long-time existence theorem for the vacuum asymptotically flat Einstein equations in the maximal slicing gauge, beyond the nearly flat small-data case?

evidence.quote: Show a long~time existence theorem for the vacuum AF Einstein equations in the maximal slicing gauge [ME]. For nearly flat initial data this is major work of Christodoulou-Klainerman [CK2].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a 4-manifold $M=\mathbb{R}\times\Sigma$, with initial data $(\Sigma,h,K)$ where $\Sigma\cong\mathbb{R}^3$, $h$ is a Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, $K$ is a symmetric 2-tensor, and $(h,K)$ are asymptotically flat (i.e., outside a compact set, in suitable coordinates, $h_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+O(|x|^{-1})$ with appropriate decay of derivatives, and $K_{ij}=O(|x|^{-2})$) and satisfy the Einstein vacuum constraint equations
$$R(h)-|K|_h^2+(\mathrm{tr}_h K)^2=0,\qquad \mathrm{div}_h K-d\,\mathrm{tr}_h K=0.$$
Evolve the data in the maximal slicing gauge: the spacetime is foliated by spacelike hypersurfaces $\Sigma_t$ of zero mean curvature ($\mathrm{tr}_h K=0$ on every leaf), with the lapse function $N$ on each leaf satisfying the elliptic equation
$$\Delta_h N = N\,|K|_h^2,\qquad N\to 1\text{ at spatial infinity}.$$
Prove a long-time (global, future-complete) existence theorem for the resulting Cauchy problem for asymptotically flat vacuum initial data that need not be a small perturbation of the trivial (Minkowski) data; that is, establish global existence of the maximal slicing foliation and the associated solution to the Einstein vacuum equations for a class of large asymptotically flat initial data strictly extending the nearly flat (small data) regime.
artifact.status_search_result: Global nonlinear stability of Minkowski space for small asymptotically flat data is established (Christodoulou–Klainerman, and subsequent work in wave coordinates by Lindblad–Rodnianski, and others). However, a long-time existence theorem in the maximal slicing gauge that extends genuinely beyond the small-data / near-Minkowski regime for asymptotically flat vacuum data does not appear to have been established; recent large-data results pertain to cosmological (CMC, expanding) settings rather than the asymptotically flat maximal-slicing problem. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Maximal Surfaces and General Relativity (Bartnik)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of maximal slicing in asymptotically flat spacetimes and difficulties of large-data global existence.
status_evidence.claim: Maximal slicing global existence beyond small data is highlighted as a difficult open question.

status_evidence.title: A large data result for vacuum Einstein's equations
status_evidence.snippet: Large-data global existence result in CMC-transported coordinates for expanding cosmological setting, not asymptotically flat maximal slicing.
status_evidence.claim: Existing large-data results apply to cosmological settings rather than the asymptotically flat maximal slicing case.

status_evidence.title: Theorems on Existence and Global Dynamics for the Einstein Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of global existence results; small-data nonlinear stability of Minkowski is the principal large-scale AF result.
status_evidence.claim: Long-time existence for AF vacuum beyond small data remains unresolved.
